senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; גשש , v. preced.) something substantial, lump, clod, ball.
units: Nidd. 23ᵃ ההיא ג׳ איקרי such a shapeless fetus is called gush (a ball, stone). Y. ib. II, 50ᵇ ג׳ של אדמה a clod of earth.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:3:17">Y. Kil. IX, 32ᵈ</cite> top; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 12:3:17">Y. Keth. XII, 35ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>ג׳ עפר</he> a handfull of Palestine earth.
<cite ref="Mishnah Tahorot 5:1">Toh. V, 1</cite> <he>ג׳ מארץ העמים</he> a lump of imported clay, v.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Challah 3:1:7">Y. Ḥall. III, 59ᵃ</cite> when the dough is formed into <he>ג׳ אחד</he> one cohesive mass; a. fr.—Pl. <he>גּוּשִׁין</he>.

<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:55">Lam. R. to I, 20</cite> (explain. <he>חמרמרו</he> <cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:55">ib.</cite>) <he>עשאן ג׳ ג׳</he> their bowels were pressed to lumps (v. <he>חמרם</he> <cite ref="Exodus 8:10">Ex. VIII, 10</cite>).

B. Mets. 101ᵃ נעקרו בגוּשֵׁיהֶן they were uprooted with their clods of earth (attached to the roots). Y. ib. VIII, end 11ᵈ [read:] בששטפן בגושיהן when the river swept them away with their clods.—גּוּשׁ חֵלֶב pr. n. pl. (Fat Ground) Gush-Heleb, Giscala (Neub. Géogr. p. 230) in Galilee.
Tosef. Men. IX, 5; a. e.—גּוּשׁ חֶלְבָּאֵי m. pl. inhabitants of Giscala. Pesik. B’shall. p. 94ᵃ; Koh. R. to XI, 2.
